item.title: Differentiating Java Development Kit (JDK), Java Runtime Environment (JRE), and Java Virtual Machine (JVM)
item.description:
“Differentiating Java Development Kit (JDK), Java Runtime Environment (JRE), and Java Virtual Machine (JVM)”

Java technology relies on three core components: the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), the Java Runtime Environment (JRE), and the Java Development Kit (JDK). While they are deeply interconnected, their roles—running code versus developing code—are distinct. When setting up a system for Java work, knowing precisely which package you need is vital for efficiency and correctness.

The Core Relationship: A Hierarchical View

A simple way to conceptualize the structure is through inclusion: the JDK is a superset, containing the JRE, which in turn contains the JVM.
